_readme: Roster and rules for the daily comment scan. Consumed by the `comment-scan` skill, which writes campaign/commentQueue via scripts/push-comment-queue.mjs. Rules here were derived by hand on 2026-08-18 and are recorded in grading-lessons.md; do not loosen them to manufacture work.
why: A reshare puts someone else's post in front of our ~0 followers. A comment puts us in front of the people already engaging with a post that is working. Out-of-network reach is earned by borrowing an audience, not by posting harder.
howToScan: Walk each target's activity page — https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>/recent-activity/all/ — and pull permalinks from the DOM. Hashtag SEARCH results carry no urn:li:activity, so nothing found there can be queued; use the feeds only to discover new names for this roster. Learned 2026-08-25. A target activity page mixes their own posts with their reshares — check for a "reposted this" line and take the byline UNDERNEATH it as the author.

timing.why: Dave is rarely at his desk before 09:30 (stated 2026-08-26), so the old 07:15 slot was a time nobody was there for. A comment's visibility still tracks the HOST post's audience — US-heavy, most active mid-morning Eastern — and 09:30 CT is 10:30 ET, which is inside that window. This is the opposite of our own posts at 19:20 CT, a different mechanic.
timing.scanBy: 05:36 CT, unattended — the queue only has to be ready before Dave is.

selection.targetShape: high reactions, LOW comments — a big audience looking and almost nobody talking
hardRules: NEVER queue a RESHARE. Open the post page and read who actually wrote it — a reshare shows the resharer at the top and the real author underneath. On 2026-08-26 a post was queued under Markus Kopko that Hiromi Nakatani wrote; the drafted comment referenced a piece of Markus own writing she had never published. Commenting on a reshare also puts us in a stranger room under a roster name, which is not the audience we chose.
The host post must still be LIVE. A two-week-old post with 200 reactions is a dead room; all-time counts mean nothing.
Skip any post already past maxHostComments — a comment is buried on arrival.
Skip video-only posts. A comment cannot be drafted without watching the video, so those are flagged for Dave to write live.
If we cannot say something true that a PMP or Security+ candidate would not already know, SKIP. No 'great post' filler, ever.

On a WIN post (someone passed), congratulate first and aim any teaching at people who will copy them — never correct the person celebrating. Dave flagged the first draft of one of these as aggressive and he was right.
Never mention CipherExam, a trial, or a link in a comment. The payoff is profile views and follows, not clicks.
Skip recruiter and job-ad posts even when the room is huge. A 440-reaction job listing has no opening for anything true about exam reasoning.
selection.lowReachException: A small room (under ~10 reactions) is still worth a comment when the host is a genuine peer and comment count is zero — yours is the only one they read. Mark those as a relationship play, not reach.

measurement.metric: profile viewers and followers, read off Dave's LinkedIn sidebar
measurement.why: The payoff from commenting is people who read it and came to look — not likes on the comment itself. Without a before-number there is nothing to compare against.

rosterHealth: Every slug below was read out of a real LinkedIn page on 2026-08-25 — none are guessed. `confidence` says how much we actually know: `proven` means we have seen the person post on-topic with measured engagement; `likely` means the profile is real and on-topic but reach is unmeasured; `unproven` means the name surfaced on a cert hashtag and nothing more. Each scan should record what it observes and DROP unproven names that never post with reach. A roster full of silent accounts wastes the scan.

targets.name: Andrew Ramdayal
targets.audience: PMP candidates — the largest on the platform
targets.note: 29 reactions / 1 comment at 23h on 2026-08-25 — the best room found that day. Every post is VIDEO, so never auto-draft: send to `manual` for Dave to watch and answer live.

targets.name: Alece Coleman, LCSW, PMP
targets.note: Posts most days. 93r/3c on a study-method post 2026-08-18 — best target that week. But the 2026-08-25 sweep found five posts in a row on career-pivot, networking and PMI-chapter topics with nothing exam-related to add. Check her, do not assume her. Scanned 2026-08-29: two live rooms (45r/7c job-search post, 42r/2c PMI Atlanta chapter call) and neither had an exam-reasoning opening. Third sweep in a row with reach but no exam topic — she posts career and chapter content, not exam content.

targets.name: Bryan Campbell
targets.note: Builds his own PM tool (PM Pixel) with ChatGPT and Claude — a genuine peer, not a competitor. Small rooms, zero comments. Relationship play; end on a question. Scanned 2026-08-29: no post in two weeks (newest 2w, 9r/1c on case-study timing). On-topic when he posts, but the cadence rarely lands inside the 5-day window.

targets.name: Markus Kopko
targets.note: GAVE US OUR ONLY TESTIMONIAL and sits on the PMI AI Standards Core Team. Build next to him, never against him — never name him as a competitor, never counter his content. His three-state self-scoring post (2026-08-20) is the structure we want to borrow, rewritten. Scanned 2026-08-29: activity page is almost all reshares; his one original (1r/1c at 1h) was a bus-factor note ending in a link to his own PM Career OS community. No exam-reasoning opening.

targets.name: Darron Clark
targets.note: Posts a PMP course series on exactly our thesis — 'the PMP exam is a judgment exam, not a memorization exam'. Sells a competing course, so add something true rather than arguing. Room was 3r/0c on 2026-08-25, below the floor. MEASURED 2026-08-29: posted the identical PMBOK-8 promo video FIVE times inside one hour, zero reactions on each. This is a broadcast account, not a room. Downgraded to priority 3 — check only for a rare non-promo post.

targets.name: Colleen E. Lofton, EdD, PMP
targets.audience: PMP candidates deciding whether to certify
targets.note: Writes 'should you get the PMP' guidance with a Substack. 7r/3c on 2026-08-19 but six days old by the time we saw it — catch her posts inside the 5-day window. Scanned 2026-08-29: 2-11 reactions on higher-ed enrolment and PMI-chapter topics; nothing exam-related inside the window.

targets.name: Dharam Singh
targets.note: 30,000 followers but the rooms are EMPTY — measured 2026-08-26: 1 to 9 reactions across five posts, zero comments, all promoting his own PMOCP and PgMP training. Follower count is vanity. Keep him only as an occasional check; do not treat the audience size as reach.

targets.name: Abhishek Sengupta
targets.note: MEASURED 2026-08-29: newest ORIGINAL post is roughly two months old and his recent rooms run 2-3 reactions. The 30K follower count buys nothing. Dormant — check rarely.

targets.name: Salina Thompson, PMP
targets.note: Launching a 'Universal PMP' podcast — PM thinking applied to life. Near-zero engagement on the teaser. Watch for whether the series finds a room. MEASURED 2026-08-29: posts daily but every room is 2-3 reactions with ZERO comments, and the content has drifted to AI-automation consulting rather than PMP. The podcast never found a room.

targets.name: Beatrice Aina, PMP
targets.note: 98r/31c on 'a PMP certification can open doors, but experience is built by walking through them'. Good reach, but comment count runs high — check it against the 20-comment cap before drafting. Scanned 2026-08-29: her big rooms (149r/18c) are all a week or older; the only in-window post was 3r/0c. Her cadence and our 5-day window rarely line up.

targets.name: Rocío Granela, PMP, CSM
targets.note: 123r/16c on a pass announcement. WIN-post rules apply: congratulate first, teach the copycats, never correct her. Scanned 2026-08-29: nothing exam-related in the window — Eldest Daughter Day and coffee posts.

targets.name: Garima Grover, PMP
targets.note: MEASURED 2026-08-29: activity page is RESHARES ONLY — her newest original post is a 2023 certification announcement. Nothing to comment on, ever. Drop at the next roster prune unless she starts writing.

targets.name: Dan Cline, P.E., PMP, PSM
targets.note: DEAD 2026-08-29: one post on the whole activity page, from 2018, 1 reaction. Remove from the roster at the next prune.

targets.name: Andrew Whitmire, PMP
targets.audience: PM job seekers — very large reach
targets.note: 440r/28c on a job listing. Big room but he posts PM ROLES, not exam content, and job ads leave no opening for anything true about exam reasoning. Keep him on the roster to catch the occasional non-job post; skip the listings. Scanned 2026-08-29: confirmed again — 460r/64c on a Museum of Ice Cream job listing, 122r/17c on a Royal Caribbean listing. Job ads with the comment count already over the cap. Evening re-sweep 2026-08-29 found the non-job post the roster keeps him for — a PMIEF International Youth Day webinar recording, 26r/2c at 4d, which clears every NUMBER in the selection rules. It was still skipped: a youth-webinar recording gives a PMP candidate no exam-reasoning opening. So the standing question about him is now answered — his non-job posts are PMIEF philanthropy, not exam content, and they will keep clearing the numbers while failing the say-something-true test.

targets.name: Torge Oeverdiek
targets.resolveBy: UNRESOLVABLE as of 2026-08-29 — LinkedIn people search for "Torge Oeverdiek" returns NO RESULTS. The poll evidence in grading-lessons.md stands on the 2026-08-11 observation; do not spend another scan hunting for this profile unless a new spelling turns up on a hashtag sweep.
targets.note: Ran a four-option question as a NATIVE POLL and got 317 votes against our comment-gate's 14 comments (observed 2026-08-11, in grading-lessons.md). Direct format competitor and the best source of poll-format evidence.

targets.name: Eric Reed
targets.note: MEASURED 2026-08-29: posts on Security+ every single day, which is the good news; the bad news is every room is 1-3 reactions with ZERO comments and most posts are adverts for his own course. Relationship play only, and not yet worth a slot.

targets.name: George Cole
targets.note: Surfaced on #SecurityPlus. Cadence and reach unmeasured. MEASURED 2026-08-29: 4-5 reactions, posts roughly weekly, mostly bootcamp promotion. Below the floor.

targets.name: Kyle Fullford, CISSP
targets.note: MEASURED 2026-08-29: newest post is a month old at 4 reactions, and his page is personal degree news (SNHU honor roll, coursework deadlines) rather than cert-prep content. Nothing to comment on as a Security+ candidate. Drop at the next roster prune unless he starts writing about the exams.

targets.name: Douglas Ogwola, CISM, CySA, SecPlus
targets.note: DEAD 2026-08-29: the entire activity page holds ONE item, a two-year-old reshare of a balloon parable. He has never posted anything of his own. Remove from the roster at the next prune.

targets.name: Jazmyn Vines
targets.note: MEASURED 2026-08-29 (evening sweep): the best target found all day and the first one this roster has produced from the Security+ side. Her mid-study post — study app, book, notes, flashcards, 'trying different ways to make sure I'm actually UNDERSTANDING the material, not just memorizing answers' — took 18r/3c in four days and ends by ASKING what helped people who already passed. That is our thesis stated by the host plus an open invitation, which is the rarest shape on the roster. Cadence is slow (previous post two weeks earlier, 5r), so she is not a daily check, but catch her study posts inside the window. Queued 2026-08-29.

targets.name: Amer Ali
targets.note: DISCOVERED 2026-08-29 on the #PMPExam latest feed. Bills himself as "The AI-Powered PMP Coach", claims 4,000+ passed, and posts exam-reasoning micro-lessons several times a day (secondary vs residual risk, contingency vs fallback) — the closest thing on the roster to our own thesis. Rooms measured at 1-6 reactions, so the reach is not there yet, and most posts are short vertical VIDEO. He sells a competing coaching product: add something true, never argue.

targets.name: Karanveer Singh, PMP, CSM, LSSGB
targets.note: DISCOVERED 2026-08-29 on the #PMPExam latest feed. Runs a daily "PMP Practice Question - Day N" series as NATIVE POLLS with A-D options — the same format competitor shape as Torge Oeverdiek and easier to observe. Measured 2026-08-29: 0-3 reactions and 12 votes on the Day 104 poll, so the format is not carrying him. Worth watching as poll-format evidence, not as a room.

targets.name: Motolani Oluwaturoti
targets.note: DISCOVERED 2026-08-29 on the #SecurityPlus latest feed — the ONLY genuine human room found on that hashtag, which is otherwise vendor spam and pay-after-you-pass proxy offers. Her Security+ pass post took 117r/33c in two days, and an earlier ISC2 post took 141r/52c. WIN-post rules apply: congratulate first, teach the copycats, never correct her. Her comment counts run HIGH and blow past the 20-comment cap fast, so she only qualifies inside the first day or so.

feeds.note: Mostly recruiters. Use for DISCOVERING names, not for queueing.
Thin, and dominated by individual cert holders rather than creators.

Alece Coleman job-environment post (45r/7c) and PMI Atlanta chapter call (42r/2c), 2026-08-29 — good rooms, no exam-reasoning opening.

Mahmoud Yousry 76-page PMP revision guide (73r/5c), queued by the morning hashtag-bar scan on a rounded 'five days' label — the urn timestamp put it at 5.17 days by the evening re-sweep, past maxHostAgeDays. DROPPED. Lesson: record postedAt from the urn, not an age string, or a post can sit in the queue a day past the live window.

Markus Kopko PgMP panel-review post (3r/1c at 6h, 2026-08-29) — on-thesis writing about the panel review being the real gate, and he is our most important relationship, but 3 reactions is under the minHostReactions floor of 5 and the single comment is his own reveal comment. The floor stands; the lowReachException wants a peer room at ZERO comments, not a self-gated one.

Amer Ali 'Most PMP practice questions can be answered without reading the scenario' (2026-08-29, 4h) — the single most on-thesis piece of writing found all day, and LinkedIn rendered NO social-counts element on it at all, meaning zero reactions. Below the floor, and he sells a competing coaching product. Watch him: if one of these ever finds a room it is the closest match on the platform.

Andrew Whitmire PMIEF youth-webinar recording (26r/2c, 4d, 2026-08-29) — clears every number in the rules and was still skipped. A webinar recording offers a PMP candidate no exam-reasoning opening, and passing the numbers is not the same as having something true to say.
